extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/agents and USPTO OED staff involved in disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and procedural standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO based on a final adjudication (e.g., state disbarment), including permissible defenses, filing deadlines, wind-up duties, publication/notice requirements, and referenced regulatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling v. Radford rebuttable presumption (due process/infirmity/grave injustice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Selling v. Radford, state disbarment creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper unless an independent review of the record reveals (1) a want of due process, (2) an infirmity of proof of the misconduct, or (3) that grave injustice would result from imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal courts generally place the burden on the respondent to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling elements precludes reciprocal discipline (citing In re Kramer).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §11.24(e) — final adjudication establishes prima facie case
rubrics_metrics.description: A final adjudication in another jurisdiction or program that a practitioner has been guilty of misconduct shall establish a prima facie case by clear and convincing evidence that the practitioner violated 37 C.F.R. 10.23, as further identified under 37 C.F.R. 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disciplinary order deemed final gives rise to the Office's prima facie case that the federal practitioner ethics rule (10.23) was violated; respondent must overcome this presumption by the standards in §11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) — grounds to avoid imposition of identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose identical discipline unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates, and the Director finds a genuine issue of material fact that one of the following exists: (i) the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process; (ii) there was such infirmity of proof as to give rise to clear conviction that the Office could not accept the conclusion; (iii) imposition of the same discipline by the Office would result in grave injustice; or (iv) any argument that the practitioner was not in fact disbarred (or similarly disciplined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the exclusive, statutory defenses the practitioner must timely raise to prevent imposition of identical discipline; the showing must be clear and convincing and create a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response requirement and required content (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order directed that if Respondent seeks to contest imposition of suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An additional 40-day extension may be granted in some circumstances (as in the August 3, 2009 notice). A mere filing of a motion to vacate the underlying state order does not, by itself, justify a stay or establish a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22 NYCRR 691.9 resignation-affidavit requirements (when resigning during investigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney who is the subject of an investigation may tender resignation via an affidavit stating: (1) resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered and not coerced; (2) the attorney is aware that there is pending an investigation into allegations of misconduct; and (3) the attorney acknowledges that if charges were predicated upon the misconduct under investigation, he could not successfully defend himself on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A resignation containing these acknowledgements may form the predicate for state disbarment; such a resignation and its contents are relevant to reciprocal-discipline proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition and wind-up duties (30 days) per 37 C.F.R. §10.40
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after that date, during which time the respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is strictly for winding up existing client matters; the respondent must take the specified withdrawal steps and comply with the referenced rule for client notification and transfer of files as required by §10.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents expansion of practice before the Office while the practitioner is being excluded and is a direct condition of the limited-recognition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and shall publish the required notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and its factual basis (including registration number, grounds, and referenced statutes and regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must set out the practitioner's name, registration number, the nature of the violation(s), and the statutory/regulatory authority for the action; disciplinary decisions are also posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room URL provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification obligation ensures other jurisdictions and courts are informed of the practitioner's exclusion and the reasons, enabling reciprocal or related actions elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 and §11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58; and shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 and 11.60 set out post-discipline responsibilities and the procedural/ substantive requirements for seeking reinstatement; compliance is mandatory as a condition of any future reinstatement consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct supporting disbarment (escrow/accounting failures; failure to cooperate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York disbarment was predicated upon respondent's affidavit of resignation acknowledging that an investigation revealed infractions of the applicable Code of Professional Responsibility regarding maintenance of attorney escrow accounts, specifically: breach of fiduciary duty with respect to attorney escrow accounts, failure to cooperate with the Grievance Committee, and failure to account for funds entrusted to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such factual findings (mismanagement of escrow, failure to account, failure to cooperate) constitute the sort of misconduct that supports a finding under 37 C.F.R. 10.23(a) and (b) and the §10.23(c)(5) route to reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to vacate state order does not by itself prevent reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's filing of a request to vacate the state court order does not, by itself, justify a stay of reciprocal discipline proceedings or a finding of a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of disbarment would result in grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a motion to vacate alone were enough, any disciplined practitioner could avoid or delay reciprocal discipline merely by seeking reconsideration; instead, the Office requires clear and convincing proof of one of the statutory defenses.
